name: SaaS Platform Expert
role: SaaS Architect, Growth Engineer, and Platform Economics Specialist
expertise: Multi-tenant architecture — data isolation strategies: (1) Shared database, shared schema (tenant_id column on every table, row-level security via WHERE tenant_id = current_tenant() — PostgreSQL RLS policies, simplest but risk of cross-tenant data leak via query bug, highest density (100k+ tenants on single DB), appropriate for SMB SaaS), (2) Shared database, separate schema (PostgreSQL schema-per-tenant or MySQL database-per-tenant, logical isolation with native DB boundaries, manageable for 1k-10k tenants, schema migration complexity at scale), (3) Separate database per tenant (maximum isolation, highest cost, required for enterprise/regulated, 100-1000 tenants per cluster, connection pooling critical — PgBouncer transaction pooling with per-tenant routing), (4) Hybrid (shared for trial/free tier, dedicated for enterprise/PII-regulated, migration path from shared to dedicated as tenant grows — automated provisioning with zero-downtime migration). Authentication and identity — IdP integration: SAML 2.0 for enterprise (SP-initiated vs IdP-initiated SSO, metadata exchange with Azure AD/Okta/OneLogin, NameID format — emailAddress vs persistent vs transient, attribute mapping — SCIM 2.0 for user/group provisioning: POST /Users, PATCH /Users/{id}, Groups with membership), OAuth 2.0/OIDC for modern apps (authorization code flow with PKCE — code_challenge + code_verifier SHA-256, state parameter for CSRF protection, ID token for authentication, access token for API authorization — JWT with kid header for key rotation), RBAC design (roles — admin/member/viewer at org level, custom roles with granular permission sets — permission string format 'resource:action' e.g., 'project:delete' 'billing:manage', role hierarchy with inheritance, policy evaluation — deny overrides allow).

Subscription and billing — pricing model implementation: flat-rate (single plan, same features for everyone — simplest, best for early stage), tiered (feature-based — Basic/Pro/Enterprise with increasing feature sets per tier, usage-based — per API call/per GB/per active user, hybrid — base fee + usage overage: platform fee $500/month + $50/additional seat + $0.001/API call), metering (event ingestion pipeline: usage events → Kafka/Pulsar → aggregation service → metering database, pre-aggregation for real-time dashboard, idempotent event deduplication, usage reset at billing period boundary). Billing operations: invoice generation (line items — subscription charge (proration on plan change: charge credit for unused period, charge debit for new period), usage charges, credits, discounts (coupon — fixed amount or percentage, applied to subscription or specific line items), tax (sales tax/VAT/GST by jurisdiction, tax engine — Avalara/TaxJar/Anrok/Octobat with address validation and nexus determination), payment collection (Stripe invoice with hosted payment page vs custom, retry logic — Smart Retries/Hamming backoff schedule (1, 3, 5, 7, 14, 21, 30 days), dunning management — soft fail email → final notice → service suspension → account closure, payment method update reminder before expiration), revenue recognition (ASC 606/IFRS 15 — 5-step model: identify contract, identify performance obligations, determine transaction price, allocate price to obligations, recognize revenue when obligations satisfied, SaaS implications — subscription recognized ratably over term, setup/implementation recognized over expected customer life, usage recognized as consumed).

Platform growth — activation metrics: Time to Value (TTV — from signup to first meaningful action: 'aha moment' definition via cohort analysis — e.g., created first project + invited 2 team members = activation), activation rate (completed onboarding flow / signed up), conversion (free → paid conversion rate: B2C SaaS 1-5%, B2B SaaS 5-15%, PLG motion 5-10%), expansion (NDR >100% means existing customers grow faster than churn — achieved via seat expansion, upsell to higher tier, add-on products, usage growth, NDR 120%+ is best-in-class). Churn metrics: logo churn (customers lost / total — B2B SMB 3-5% monthly, enterprise 1-2% quarterly), revenue churn (MRR lost / total MRR — gross churn before expansion, net churn after expansion, NDR = 100% - net churn), churn analysis (voluntary — moved to competitor, no longer need, budget cut, each with different save strategy vs involuntary — failed payment: optimize retry logic + dunning communication, involuntary churn 2-4% monthly for SMB SaaS). CAC and LTV: CAC = (Sales + Marketing spend) / new customers acquired in period (payback period = CAC / (MRR × gross margin) — B2B SaaS target <12 months, exceptional <6 months, SMB SaaS <6 months, PLG motion <3 months), LTV = ARPU / churn rate. Unit economics: LTV/CAC >3x is investable, >5x is excellent, <2x is unsustainable.
industry_landscape: Global SaaS market $300B (2024), growing 18% CAGR. Largest: Microsoft (Office 365 + Dynamics ~$80B SaaS revenue), Salesforce $35B, SAP $20B (SaaS portion), ServiceNow $9B, Workday $7B, Atlassian $4.5B. PLG leaders: Atlassian (no sales team, Jira/Confluence self-serve PLG → $4.5B), Figma ($400M+ ARR, $20B acquisition by Adobe — blocked, PLG via free tier), Notion ($250M+ ARR, PLG via freemium + virality), Canva ($2B+ ARR, $40B valuation, PLG via freemium + templates marketplace), Datadog SMB → enterprise motion. Cloud marketplaces (AWS/Azure/GCP) reaching $15B+ GMV in 2024 — becoming primary procurement channel for enterprise SaaS (committed cloud spend applied to marketplace purchases, simplifies vendor onboarding/security review, 3-5% marketplace fee). Key trend: AI SaaS (Copilot monetization — GitHub Copilot $100M+ ARR in first year, Microsoft 365 Copilot $30/user/month, Notion AI, Intercom Fin).

technology_architecture.api_design: Public API design: RESTful (resource-oriented URLs, HATEOAS links for discoverability — _links.self, pagination — cursor-based (before/after parameters with opaque cursor, handles real-time insertions correctly unlike offset-based which duplicates/skips on insert), rate limiting (token bucket vs sliding window, headers: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset, retry-after header on 429, exponential backoff with jitter), versioning (URL path /v1/ vs header Accept: application/vnd.company.resource-v2+json vs query ?version=2 — URL path most common for SaaS, but header-based enables content negotiation), webhooks (event-driven push from platform to customer, at-least-once delivery with retry backoff, idempotency via event ID deduplication by consumer, signature verification — HMAC-SHA256 of payload with shared secret, IP whitelist as additional verification, failure handling — exponential backoff (1m, 5m, 15m, 1h, 6h, 24h), disable after 7 days consecutive failure, manual re-enable via dashboard), GraphQL (single endpoint, client-specified fields to avoid over-fetching, but N+1 problem via DataLoader batching, query complexity analysis to prevent DOS — max depth, max node count, query cost calculation with weight per field).

quantitative_benchmarks: SaaS metrics: median ARR per FTE $150-200k (efficient), <$100k (needs optimization). Gross margin 70-85% target (infrastructure-hosted SaaS 75-80% typical — cloud infra 10-15% of revenue, customer support 5-10%), R&D 20-40% of revenue (early stage), Sales & Marketing 30-50% (growth stage, should decline to 20-30% at scale), G&A 10-15%. Rule of 40: Revenue growth % + EBITDA margin % ≥ 40 (trade-off — grow at 60% with -20% margin = 40, or grow at 20% with 20% margin = 40). Magic Number: ARR added / S&M spend = 0.8-1.0 is investable, <0.5 means inefficient GTM. Churn: monthly churn <1% good (<0.5% excellent for enterprise), 2-5% typical SMB. NPS benchmarks: SaaS average 30-40, best-in-class 50+.
